## F01 Loop and built-in tools

- F01.loop-shape — Loop shape [supported, verified] The core interprets tool use requests from the Gemini model and returns tool execution results to the model for further processing. A `continue` field set to `false` kills the entire agent loop immediately. Automatic detection and prevention of infinite loops can be disabled via a setting. | ev: E-gemini-cli-00370, E-gemini-cli-00371, E-gemini-cli-00458, E-gemini-cli-00303
- F01.turn-limits — Turn and step limits [supported, unverified] `model.maxSessionTurns` caps the user/model/tool turns kept in a session (-1 means unlimited). A subagent's `max_turns` field caps conversation turns before it must return (defaults to 30). `maxActionsPerTask` caps tool calls per task; the agent is terminated when the limit is reached. Exit code 53 means the session turn maximum was reached (non-interactive mode only). | ev: E-gemini-cli-00301, E-gemini-cli-00423, E-gemini-cli-00405, E-gemini-cli-02103
- F01.tool-inventory — Native tool inventory [supported, unverified] `grep_search` searches file contents for a regular expression (legacy alias `search_file_content`). The core registers available tools (for example, file system tools, shell command ...). `/tools` displays the tools currently available. A setting restricts the set of built-in tools with an allowlist. | ev: E-gemini-cli-00794, E-gemini-cli-00369, E-gemini-cli-00598, E-gemini-cli-00673
- F01.shell-tool — Shell execution tool [supported, unverified] `run_shell_command` lets the Gemini model execute commands; it executes arbitrary shell commands, supports interactive sessions and background processes, and requires manual confirmation. - F01.file-edit-tools — File read, edit and write tools [supported, unverified] Core provides a suite of file system tools. Gemini uses the `glob` or `list_directory` tools to search the project; `@` commands use `read_many_files` internally. ## F09 Subagents and custom agents

- F09.tool-allowlist — Tool allow-list [supported, unverified] The optional tools frontmatter array lists tool names the agent can use; wildcards are * (all tools), mcp_* (all MCP tools) and mcp_server_* (all tools from a server). If omitted, it inherits all tools from the parent session. The subagent only has access to the tools you explicitly (quote truncated). Even with the * wildcard it is unable to see or invoke other agents. | ev: E-gemini-cli-00419, E-gemini-cli-00498, E-gemini-cli-00499, E-gemini-cli-00428

## F12 MCP

- F12.client-support — Client support [supported, verified] Gemini CLI works with MCP servers: `/mcp` manages configured Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, MCP resource tools let it discover and retrieve data, and `list_mcp_resources` lists all available resources exposed by connected MCP servers. In tool execution, arguments are validated against the tool's schema. | ev: E-gemini-cli-00477, E-gemini-cli-00799, E-gemini-cli-02137, E-gemini-cli-00985
- F12.transports — Transports [partial, verified] Stdio transport spawns a subprocess and communicates via stdin/stdout; SSE transport connects to Server-Sent Events endpoints; `httpUrl` is the URL of an MCP server that uses streamable HTTP transport. | limit: Admin-required MCP servers: 'Required servers only support remote transports (`sse`, `http`).' | ev: E-gemini-cli-02215, E-gemini-cli-02216, E-gemini-cli-00729, E-gemini-cli-01058
- F12.config-scope — Config location and scope [supported, unverified] MCP servers are configured through the `mcpServers` configuration in `settings.json`, which Gemini CLI loads from three levels (System, Workspace, and a third). The MCP tutorial opens `~/.gemini/settings.json` (or a project-specific one). An extension's `gemini-extension.json` can also carry `mcpServers`, a map of MCP servers to settings. | ev: E-gemini-cli-02223, E-gemini-cli-01503, E-gemini-cli-02320, E-gemini-cli-01330
- F12.auth — Authentication [supported, verified] `/mcp` includes an operation to 'Authenticate with an OAuth-enabled MCP server'. An MCP server's `headers` property sets custom HTTP headers when using `url` or `httpUrl`. In the Required MCP Servers (preview) section, an optional `oauth` object includes `scopes` and `clientId`, and an optional `authProviderType` field names the authentication provider. | ev: E-gemini-cli-00478, E-gemini-cli-02232, E-gemini-cli-01060, E-gemini-cli-01059
- F12.tool-filtering — Tool filtering and naming [supported, unverified] Restricting tools within an MCP server is done using the `includeTools` and `excludeTools` properties. The `--allowed-mcp-server-names` flag takes allowed MCP server names (comma-separated or multiple flags). An MCP tool's registered name is potentially prefixed. In the policy engine, `mcp_server_*` matches any tool from a specific MCP server. | ev: E-gemini-cli-01506, E-gemini-cli-00011, E-gemini-cli-00978, E-gemini-cli-00808
- F12.server-trust — Server trust and approval [supported, unverified] Administrators can define an explicit allowlist of MCP servers. The --allowed-mcp-server-names flag takes allowed MCP server names (comma-separated or multiple flags). By default, read-only MCP tools require user confirmation in Plan Mode. Each DiscoveredMCPTool implements sophisticated confirmation logic. | ev: E-gemini-cli-01045, E-gemini-cli-00011, E-gemini-cli-00226, E-gemini-cli-00979

## F13 Sessions, checkpoints, rewind

- F13.resume-continue — Resume and continue [supported, unverified] The --resume (-r) flag resumes a previous session; use "latest" for the most recent or an index number (for example --resume 5). /chat is an alias for /resume. Session management saves your conversation history so you can resume your work. | ev: E-gemini-cli-00014, E-gemini-cli-00463, E-gemini-cli-01581
- F13.fork-branch — Fork or branch a session [supported, unverified] Save the current state with /resume save decision-point, then use /resume resume decision-point to fork the conversation back. This creates a new branch of history without losing your original work. Chat checkpoints give named branch points inside a session. | ev: E-gemini-cli-02359, E-gemini-cli-02360, E-gemini-cli-02358, E-gemini-cli-01591
- F13.checkpoint-rewind — Checkpoint and rewind [supported, verified] The /rewind command lets you go back to a previous state in your conversation. A Checkpointing feature automatically saves a snapshot, and a setting is described as "Enable session checkpointing for recovery". Manual tagged checkpoints support list, save, resume, delete and share subcommands. | ev: E-gemini-cli-01555, E-gemini-cli-01416, E-gemini-cli-00621, E-gemini-cli-00464
- F13.transcript-storage — Transcript storage [supported, verified] By default, Gemini CLI stores configuration and history in ~/.gemini. Every session is recorded locally as a transcript. A transcript_path field is documented as an absolute path to the session transcript JSON. Chats are saved into a project-specific directory. | ev: E-gemini-cli-01501, E-gemini-cli-01855, E-gemini-cli-01371, E-gemini-cli-00466
- F13.session-listing — Session naming and listing [supported, unverified] The --list-sessions flag lists available sessions for the current project and exits. A searchable list of all your past sessions can be opened; press / to enter search mode, then type to filter sessions by ID. | ev: E-gemini-cli-00015, E-gemini-cli-02348, E-gemini-cli-01590
- F13.cross-surface-handoff — Cross-surface handoff [partial, verified] A changelog entry lists "Session Export and Import" and says it "Added the ability to export sessions to files". | limit: Documented as the ability to export sessions to files. | ev: E-gemini-cli-01090

## F17 Model selection and routing

- F17.model-picker — Model picker [supported, verified] The `/model` command lets you configure the model Gemini CLI uses, and its reference entry says it 'Opens a dialog to configure the model'. The changelog describes it as choosing the Gemini model for your session. The Gemini 3 page says to use `/model` and select Manual to check access to Gemini 3.1. | ev: E-gemini-cli-00086, E-gemini-cli-00481, E-gemini-cli-00145, E-gemini-cli-00441
- F17.model-flag-env — Flag, setting and environment [supported, verified] The --model (-m) flag chooses the model (default `auto`). The `model.name` setting sets the Gemini model used for conversations (default `undefined`). Model selection follows a defined order of precedence. | ev: E-gemini-cli-00020, E-gemini-cli-00300, E-gemini-cli-00637, E-gemini-cli-00080
- F17.auto-routing — Automatic routing [supported, verified] Gemini CLI model routing intelligently picks the best model, and also switches to a fallback model on model failure (enabled by default). general.plan.modelRouting switches between Pro (planning) and Flash (implementation) based on Plan Mode status. When the default pro model is rate-limited, it automatically switches to flash for the current session. | ev: E-gemini-cli-00146, E-gemini-cli-00074, E-gemini-cli-00285, E-gemini-cli-00374
- F17.provider-byok — Providers and bring-your-own-key [partial, verified] A Gemini API key is an alternative if you don't want to authenticate using your Google account. billing.vertexAi.requestType sets the X-Vertex-AI-LLM-Request-Type header for Vertex AI requests. - F17.model-catalog — Model catalog and availability [supported, verified] The /model dialog's Auto (Gemini 3) option picks among gemini-3-pro-preview and gemini-3-flash-preview. The auto alias is the default and resolves to the preview model if preview features are enabled, otherwise to the standard pro model. experimental.gemma enables Gemma 4 models via Gemini API. Unpaid Gemini API key requests go to the Flash model only. | ev: E-gemini-cli-00089, E-gemini-cli-00021, E-gemini-cli-00330, E-gemini-cli-00950

## F19 Modes and autonomy levels

- F19.named-modes — Named modes [supported, verified] Tool-execution approval modes are default, auto_edit, yolo and plan (--approval-mode). default prompts for approval, auto_edit auto-approves edit tools, plan is read-only; YOLO (auto-approve all actions) is enabled only via command line. Shift+Tab cycles default, auto_edit and plan. | ev: E-gemini-cli-00001, E-gemini-cli-00280, E-gemini-cli-00789, E-gemini-cli-00821
- F19.entering-modes — How modes are entered [supported, verified] Shift+Tab cycles approval modes default, auto_edit and plan (plan is skipped when the agent is busy). Setting Default Approval Mode to Plan starts in Plan Mode. --approval-mode=yolo is used instead of --yolo (the two cannot be used together). The enter_plan_mode tool switches the CLI to a safe, read-only Plan Mode. | ev: E-gemini-cli-00789, E-gemini-cli-00097, E-gemini-cli-00769, E-gemini-cli-00801
- F19.plan-mode — Plan mode [supported, verified] Plan Mode is a read-only environment for architecting solutions before implementation; the plan approval mode is a strict read-only mode for research and design. A command switches to Plan Mode (read-only) and shows the current plan if one has been generated. Executing a plan switches from plan mode to active execution. | ev: E-gemini-cli-00093, E-gemini-cli-00823, E-gemini-cli-00576, E-gemini-cli-00348
- F19.autonomy-mode — Auto-accept and autonomous modes [partial, verified] --approval-mode=yolo auto-approves all actions (the --yolo flag is deprecated). auto_edit auto-approves edit tools. Ctrl+Y toggles YOLO (auto-approval) mode for tool calls. autoEdit is optimized for automated code editing. | limit: YOLO mode (auto-approve all actions) can only be enabled via command line (--yolo or --approval-mode=yolo) (E-gemini-cli-00281); the keyboard page lists a Ctrl+Y toggle (E-gemini-cli-00790), so the scope of 'only' is unreconciled. | ev: E-gemini-cli-00002, E-gemini-cli-00281, E-gemini-cli-00790, E-gemini-cli-00822
- F19.read-only-mode — Read-only or ask mode [supported, verified] Plan Mode is a read-only environment for designing solutions before implementation. The plan approval mode is a strict read-only mode for research and design, and in Plan Mode the agent is restricted to read-only tools. | ev: E-gemini-cli-00093, E-gemini-cli-00823, E-gemini-cli-00966, E-gemini-cli-00118
- F19.mode-defaults — Mode defaults and persistence [supported, verified] general.defaultApprovalMode defaults to 'default', which prompts for approval on each tool call; the setting also covers auto_edit and plan. Plan Mode is enabled by default (as of v0.34.0) and can be managed via /settings. | ev: E-gemini-cli-00280, E-gemini-cli-00764, E-gemini-cli-00095, E-gemini-cli-01116

## F22 Usage, cost, limits and observability

- F22.usage-visibility — Usage and cost visibility [supported, unverified] Token usage and cached token savings can be viewed with /stats. The headless JSON output carries a stats object with token usage and API latency metrics. A summary of model usage is presented on exit at the end of a session. Cached token information is only displayed when cached tokens are being used. | ev: E-gemini-cli-01676, E-gemini-cli-01527, E-gemini-cli-02091, E-gemini-cli-02075
- F22.budget-caps — Budgets and caps [partial, verified] billing.overageStrategy sets how to handle quota exhaustion when AI credits are available: 'ask' prompts each time, 'always' automatically uses credits, 'never' disables credit usage. The default is "ask". | limit: Scoped to "quota exhaustion when AI credits are available"; the options are ask (prompt each time), always (automatically use credits) or never (disable credit usage). | ev: E-gemini-cli-00299, E-gemini-cli-00635
- F22.rate-limits — Rate-limit behaviour [supported, verified] For Log in with Google (Gemini Code Assist for individuals), the listed limit is 1000 maximum model requests / user / day. When rate-limited, the CLI automatically switches to the "flash" model. It tells you when you reach your Gemini 3 Pro daily usage limit. A 429 Resource exhausted error indicates the API request limit was exceeded. | ev: E-gemini-cli-00947, E-gemini-cli-00374, E-gemini-cli-00444, E-gemini-cli-02074
- F22.telemetry-otel — Telemetry and OpenTelemetry [supported, verified] Gemini CLI uses OpenTelemetry (OTel) to record traces that help debug agent behavior. - F22.logs-debug — Logs and debug output [supported, unverified] --debug (-d) runs in debug mode with verbose logging (default false). /chat debug exports the most recent API request as a JSON payload.
